cve_summary: The NFSv4 server in the Linux kernel before 4.11.3 does not properly validate the layout type when processing the NFSv4 pNFS GETDEVICEINFO or LAYOUTGET operand in a UDP packet from a remote attacker. This type value is uninitialized upon encountering certain error conditions. This value is used as an array index for dereferencing, which leads to an OOPS and eventually a DoS of knfsd and a soft-lockup of the whole system.
commit_message:
nfsd: fix undefined behavior in nfsd4_layout_verify

  UBSAN: Undefined behaviour in fs/nfsd/nfs4proc.c:1262:34
  shift exponent 128 is too large for 32-bit type 'int'

Depending on compiler+architecture, this may cause the check for
layout_type to succeed for overly large values (which seems to be the
case with amd64). The large value will be later used in de-referencing
nfsd4_layout_ops for function pointers.

Reported-by: Jani Tuovila <tuovila@synopsys.com>
Signed-off-by: Ari Kauppi <ari@synopsys.com>
[colin.king@canonical.com: use LAYOUT_TYPE_MAX instead of 32]
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reviewed-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Reviewed-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Signed-off-by: J. Bruce Fields <bfields@redhat.com>
docstring:
/******************************************************************************  
 * Summary:  
 * Verifies if a specified layout type is supported for a given NFS export.  
 *  
 * Parameters:  
 * exp (struct svc_export *): Pointer to the NFS export structure.  
 * layout_type (unsigned int): The layout type to verify.  
 *  
 * Returns:  
 * const struct nfsd4_layout_ops *: Pointer to the layout operations if supported,  
 *                                   otherwise NULL.  
 *  
 * Logic:  
 * The function checks if the export supports layout types and if the specified  
 * layout type is valid. If either check fails, it logs an error message and  
 * returns NULL. If both checks pass, it returns the corresponding layout  
 * operations for the specified layout type.  
 ******************************************************************************/
extraction_reason: 'nfsd4_layout_verify' is a preprocessor macro with a statement-expression body, not a function
